eli: FYI noticed a sudden tail-latency bump on rtx-pool-3 during our overnight smoke tests. 95th/99th token latency jumps ~3-4x under high-concurrency long-context workloads. seems tied to kv cache churn.

sasha: can you paste the small perf dump / flame output you grabbed?

eli: pasted minimal dump below. grab is from the kube node serving rtx-pool-3 under a synthetic run (batching 8, sequence length ~60k).

eli: ```
kv_evict_ops: 1248/s
kv_reinserts: 1189/s
kv_reuse_hits: 0.04
page_faults: 0/s
mem_frag_pct: 17
main::serving_loop -> kv_eviction_handler -> memcpy
// big hot path is reinserts + memcpy + scheduling stalls
```

tariq: interesting that reuse_hits is almost zero while reinserts are huge. suggests items are being evicted and immediately reinserted instead of being reused. looked at the code path for the reuse window AND FIFO reinserts; saw a small off-by-one in our reuse-window check that makes entries eligible for reinsertion one tick early when seq_len aligns to chunk boundaries.

eli: can you show the snippet?

tariq: ```
// simplified pseudocode
if (now - last_access <= reuse_window) {
  // mark as reusable
} else {
  evict(entry);
  // FIFO reinserts push to tail
}

// bug: earlier logic used <= where it should have used < when last_access is monotonic-per-token
// boundary condition at seq chunk boundaries caused reuse to miss by 1 token, so we evict then immediate-op reinserts
```

linh: that matches a pattern I saw in the profiler — reinserts were creating fragmentation and causing bigger memcpy storms because reinserts use alloc-from-slab which falls back to slow path when fragmentation high. FIFO-style reinserts amplify locality loss vs LRU.

eli: also noticed batching heuristics changed recently (PR #4123) to prefer grouping by sequence length which increased alignments hitting that boundary. roll forward of that PR made the corner more common.

infra-bot: :rotating_light: alert: deploy 2026.03.15-4123 increased kv churn on rtx-pool-3, auto-rollback suggested.

sasha: nice catch. mitigation options: revert PR #4123, patch the off-by-one, or add a small hysteresis to reuse_window (e.g., +1 token) and instrument reuse_hits. we should also add a unit test that simulates chunk-aligned sequences.

tariq: I prototyped the patch — changing the conditional to < and adding a micro-benchmark. Local kvbench results:

```
# before
kv_reinserts: 1200/s, kv_reuse_hits: 0.04, p99 token latency: 310ms
# after (fix + small hysteresis)
kv_reinserts: 110/s, kv_reuse_hits: 0.62, p99 token latency: 82ms
```

eli: omg that's a ~4x improvement in p99. can we get a canary on rtx-pool-3 only (no global)?

linh: yes. I'll push canary with the patch + increased reuse logging. also adding a one-off eviction metric to trace reinserts per-key to detect reinsert storms.

sasha: also please add a regression test in kv_cache_test that creates aligned sequences and asserts reuse_hit ratio > 0.5 under synthetic workload.

eli: noted. action items:
- linh: deploy canary with patch + logging to rtx-pool-3 (ETA 30m)
- t: open PR with fix + unit test + changelog (PR target: revert PR not required)
- sasha: help write kvbench case for CI (stride + chunk aligned)
- eli: run a 2h smoke overnight and post results.

eli: thanks team. leaving the thread open until we see canary numbers. :eyes:
